text:
viv: Heads-up: we need a short, operator-friendly runbook for degrading dedicated GPU pools gracefully. Postmortem showed operator confusion and a couple bad manual fixes.

omar: Agreed. We should standardize the stages and make them reversible with clear console flags.

rachel: Observed failure chain: tenant X spike -> prewarm credit exhaustion -> eviction churn -> scale-up blocked by MIG fragmentation. We need a plan that handles both request routing and packing.

viv: My proposal: a 4-phase plan: detect -> stabilize -> prioritize -> spill. Names: detect, stabilize, prioritize, spillover.

miko: quick defs pls.

viv: detect: metrics-based alert (p95, token-drop, prewarm-fail rate).

stabilize: conservative runtime tweaks (reduce batching, disable nonessential caches).

prioritize: admission policy change (allow only SLA_high + SLA_gold by default), enable soft-preemptible lanes.

spillover: route X% of traffic to hosted/quantized variants with per-tenant throttles.

omar: Add small random jitter before executing stabilize/prioritize to avoid multiple pools doing the same thing simultaneously.

rachel: Triggers: sliding-window p95 > 1s AND prewarm_fail_rate > 5% for 20s. Hysteresis: require normal metrics for 60s before rollback.

miko: On the MIG issue: we should attempt a packing-reset that prefers fewer fractional MIG allocations before we trigger scale-up — this buys time. Add to stabilize.

ops-bot: incident 2026-04-02-08 created: https://incidents.internal/2026-04-02-08 :rotating_light:

sam: runbook ops commands (sketch):
`/poolctl stage set eu-central detect --reason "high-p95"`
`/poolctl stage set eu-central stabilize --duration 10m`
`/poolctl spillroute add eu-central tenant=tenant-x pct=5 variant=hosted-quant8`

devrel: Policy schema draft (YAML) — lean fields only:

```yaml
policy_version: 1
degrade_on:
  p95_ms: 1000
  prewarm_fail_pct: 5
  window_seconds: 20
hysteresis_seconds: 60
stages:
  - id: stabilize
    runtime_changes:
      batch_scale: 0.7
      cache_factor: 0.6
      packing_reset: true
  - id: prioritize
    admission:
      allow: [sla_high, sla_gold]
      preemptible: true
  - id: spillover
    routing:
      fraction_default: 0.05
      max_per_tenant: 0.15
      target_variant: quant8-hosted
```

viv: Nice. A few operational constraints: 1) block scale-downs while any degradation stage active; 2) keep audit log for manual commands; 3) surface expected cost impact when spillover enabled.

omar: We should also expose a degradation token in the admission response so clients can metric-emit which fallback they hit (helps debugging).

rachel: For tenant-aware routing, implement a token-bucket per-tenant so big tenants don't consume entire spill budget.

miko: I'll add a tiny local simulator in the autoscaler repo to reproduce packing edgecases (fractional-MIG + racey placement). If we can repro CI failures we can catch regressions.

sam: Add tests: unit for schema validation + e2e sim for stage transitions under synthetic spikes.

viv: Action items:
- omar: concrete metric thresholds and jitter windows (owner: omar)
- miko: packing-reset algorithm + simulator (owner: miko)
- rachel: tenant-bucket design and admission token (owner: rachel)
- devrel: add cost estimate fields to policy + console surface (owner: devrel)
- sam: runbook CLI snippets and audit log hooks (owner: sam)

viv: I'll draft the short RFC follow-up and attach the runbook and YAML examples. Planning a 30m sync tomorrow. Please @me when PRs are ready. :thumbsup:
